title: Business Context & Analytics Objectives
summary: Transforming high-velocity raw ecommerce clickstream logs into structured, explainable commercial intelligence without making unsupported predictive assumptions.
key_points: Modern ecommerce platforms generate tens of millions of raw interaction logs monthly that overwhelm traditional relational databases.
The analytical objective was to analyze user engagement, temporal purchasing rhythms, catalog brand concentration, and customer segmentation on historical October 2019 data.
Enforced strict descriptive governance: avoiding synthetic recommender claims, speculative customer lifetime value calculations, or unsupported currency inferences.
technical_details: Input data scope: October 1 to November 1, 2019 (UTC)
Target metrics: Total event volume, gross recorded revenue, unique users, session counts, and brand concentration
Governance policy: Every metric must trace directly to verified Spark/CSV outputs

title: Raw Telemetry Ingestion & HDFS Architecture
summary: Ingesting 42,448,764 raw clickstream rows (~5.6 GB) into distributed Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) across 13 partitions.
key_points: Raw event telemetry captures micro-actions: page views, shopping cart additions, and confirmed purchases.
Distributed across Hadoop DataNodes with a replication factor of 3 (16.8 GB total cluster footprint) ensuring zero data loss.
Established 128 MB block allocation for optimal MapReduce parallel task scheduling.
technical_details: Source schema: event_time, event_type, product_id, category_id, category_code, brand, price, user_id, user_session
Storage path: hdfs:///ecommerce/raw/2019-Oct.csv
Initial record count: 42,448,764 rows

title: Distributed Big-Data Processing with Apache Spark
summary: Leveraging PySpark's distributed in-memory computing engine to execute parallelized transformations across multi-node clusters.
key_points: Single-node Python tools (Pandas) encounter out-of-memory crashes on multi-gigabyte event streams.
PySpark DataFrame API distributes execution DAGs across cluster workers with lazy evaluation and memory caching.
Optimized shuffle partitions and co-located compute tasks directly with HDFS storage blocks.
technical_details: Engine: Apache Spark 3.x with Catalyst Query Optimizer
Partition count: 13 distributed RDD partitions aligned with HDFS block splits
Execution model: Resilient Distributed Datasets (RDD) with in-memory columnar caching

title: Data Quality Cleaning & Anomaly Hygiene
summary: Filtering 68,673 non-positive prices and 30,217 unsegregated malformed records, retaining 42,349,874 verified events (99.77% retention).
key_points: Eliminated 68,673 records logged with price <= 0.00 to guarantee financial integrity.
Quarantined 30,217 unsegregated multi-condition removal records (unparseable formats, timestamp errors).
Preserved 13.5M unclassified categories and 6.1M unbranded products as explicit 'Unknown' tokens to protect GMV totals without artificial imputation.
Executed distributed dropDuplicates() pass to eliminate redundant network retries.
technical_details: Net records removed: 98,890 (0.233% of raw volume)
Verified cleaned count: 42,349,874 records
Storage output: hdfs:///ecommerce/cleaned/2019-Oct.parquet (1.4 GB Snappy compressed)

title: Analytical Aggregations & Temporal Rollups
summary: Executing distributed MapReduce group-by rollups to synthesize temporal, category, and brand summaries totaling 229,933,212.63 monetary units.
key_points: Discovered 7-hour temporal decoupling: browsing peaks at 21:00 UTC (3.05M events) while purchasing peaks at 14:00 UTC (17.5M units).
Identified massive category concentration: Electronics (72.38%) and Appliances (17.92%) drive over 90.3% of platform GMV.
Quantified brand Pareto dynamics: top 10 commercial brands capture 81.65% of recorded brand revenue, led by Apple (47.57%) and Samsung (18.78%).
technical_details: Precomputed artifacts: 12 summary CSV tables published for dashboard visualization
Verified revenue invariant: Category sum = Weekday sum = Daily sum = 229,933,212.63 units
Total purchase transactions: 742,773 events

title: User-Level Behavioral Feature Engineering
summary: Aggregating 42.35M events into 11 behavioral feature vectors for 3,021,435 distinct users to characterize individual interaction intensity.
key_points: Aggregated per-user metrics: total events, views, carts, purchases, gross spend, average price, session counts, and catalog breadth.
Applied log1p(x) transformation to right-skewed monetary metrics, successfully reducing price skewness from +2.54 to -0.27.
Normalized all 11 features using StandardScaler to zero mean and unit variance.
technical_details: Analyzed user population: 3,021,435 initial user profiles
Feature matrix dimension: 3,021,435 rows x 11 standardized features
Output artifact: hdfs:///ecommerce/results/user_features_corrected

title: PCA Dimensionality Reduction (95.97% Variance)
summary: Eigen-decomposing the 11x11 correlation matrix into 7 orthogonal principal components, retaining 95.967% of cumulative behavioral variance.
key_points: Eliminated multicollinearity among highly correlated features (views, sessions, and events).
PC1 (40.71%) and PC2 (17.93%) capture 58.64% of total behavioral variance.
Pruned components 8 through 11, reducing dimensionality by 36.4% while preserving 95.97% of variance.
technical_details: PCA model: PySpark MLlib PCA implementation
Cumulative variance progression: PC1 40.71% -> PC2 58.64% -> PC3 73.40% -> PC4 81.83% -> PC5 87.63% -> PC6 92.14% -> PC7 95.97%
Scientific disclaimer: Component axes represent linear algebraic factor weights, not physical or psychological laws

title: K-Means Customer Segmentation (K=2, Silhouette 0.81115)
summary: Partitioning 3,021,434 users in 7D PCA space into an active commercial core (8.29%) and a casual browsing majority (91.71%), quarantining 1 extreme outlier.
key_points: Tested 6 sensitivity trials (K=2 to K=5); K=2 achieved the optimal silhouette score of 0.81115 (exceeding the 0.80 literature reference heuristic).
Quarantined 1 extreme browsing outlier account (7,429 views, 0 purchases) to prevent centroid pull.
Cluster 0 Core (250,388 users) averages 520.86 units spend (14.5x higher) and 1.58 purchases (12.6x higher) compared to Cluster 1 Browsers (2,771,046 users, 35.91 units spend, 0.125 purchases).
technical_details: Selected model: K=2 Outlier Excluded (3,021,434 evaluated users)
Silhouette score: 0.81115 (vs 0.51978 for K=3, 0.57195 for K=4)
Centroid validation: Evaluated in original business units via inverse scaling

title: Visualization & Dashboard Architecture
summary: Re-engineering the legacy Python Streamlit dashboard into a high-performance React + TypeScript web application with modular Apache ECharts and Three.js.
key_points: Streamlit suffers from full-script re-executions on every user interaction, slow canvas resizing, and rigid layout constraints.
Modern React architecture delivers sub-16ms interactive renders, client-side route code splitting, and fully responsive layouts.
Reimplemented legacy Plotly charts natively in Apache ECharts, preserving exact analytical meaning with superior rendering performance.
technical_details: Framework: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite 5 + Tailwind CSS
Visualization: Apache ECharts 5.5 + Three.js WebGL spatial anchor (sustained 60 FPS, avg 16.6ms)
State management: Modular React hooks with zero-dependency typed JSON data contracts

title: Research Boundaries & Reproducibility Disclosures
summary: Documenting analytical boundaries, calendar anomalies, telemetry limitations, and currency neutrality to ensure full scientific transparency.
key_points: Currency neutrality: Telemetry prices are reported in neutral monetary units; currency symbols ($, ₹) are strictly excluded.
Calendar caveat: November 1 record represents a partial logging day (8,065 orders) before dataset cutoff.
Clustering boundaries: Descriptive historical segmentation does not imply predictive customer lifetime value or real-time conversion propensity.
Deduplication caveat: 30,217 unsegregated remainder rows reflect multi-condition cleaning filters from historical PySpark execution.
technical_details: Reproducibility: All 35 master data invariants validated via automated test scripts (npm run validate-data)
Unit testing: 41 automated Vitest unit tests verifying data integrity across all views
Documentation suite: Comprehensive architectural audit reports maintained in docs/commerceiq/
